_doc: Roads to victory (Systems/Victory.cs). Every road ends the big bad's threat in its own way, so none can be claimed before the big bad has shown itself (been crowned). Slay is the Saga's own finale (Saga.Win). Once its terms hold the mayor may claim it (Simulation.ClaimRoad): the big bad marches at once, and the terms must hold `hold` days more. Numbers: allies = allied settlements and powers; powers = minor powers allied; sworn = standing a settlement needs to count as under the banner; fameTier = notoriety.json fame tier index (3 Renowned, 4 Legendary); tier = city.json charter id; cleared = share of known sites cleared; income = trade gold over the last month; liberty = the form of government's liberty at least (commonwealth) or at most (crown); moots = yearly moots held; content = share of the town (by bloc size) whose blocs feel well of the mayor; trust = the town's trust in the mayor's word; ruled = days under the present form; watch = the watch's strength.

roads.name: Slay the Big Bad
roads.blurb: Your heroes hunt down and kill the villain behind it all.
roads.title: The Long Night is over

roads.name: Grand Alliance
roads.blurb: Your allies' combined might makes the big bad a spent force.
roads.title: The Grand Alliance stands
roads.ending: The banners of {allies} allies gather under {town}'s. Counted against them, {name} is a spent force: {leader} sues for terms, gives up {seat} and is never heard of again.

roads.name: Dominion
roads.blurb: Every settlement and minor power flies your banner.
roads.title: One banner over the wilds
roads.ending: From the hills to the far roads every hall flies {town}'s banner. With no one left to shelter or arm it, {name} is hunted from valley to valley until {leader} is taken in chains.

roads.name: Age of Legends
roads.blurb: Your heroes grow so famous that the big bad's servants desert it.
roads.title: An age of legends
roads.ending: Songs of {town}'s heroes are sung in {leader}'s own camp. One by one its captains slip away to join the legend, until {name} is a name for frightening children and nothing more.

roads.name: Golden Age
roads.blurb: A great city rich, content and safe, even with the big bad at the gates.
roads.title: A golden age
roads.ending: Through the worst {name} could do, {town} has known nothing but plenty. {name}'s own people slip away to its gates for bread and work, until {leader} rules an empty land and is heard of no more.

roads.name: Free Commonwealth
roads.blurb: A free town whose people choose their council and their mayor, content and trusting, year after year.
roads.title: The free commonwealth
roads.ending: {name} sends heralds to {town} to call for surrender, and the moot votes them down to a man. Word of a town where every household has its say runs through the wilds faster than {leader}'s riders, and the folk of {name}'s own lands slip away to it. A tyrant can't hold a land whose people have seen the alternative: {leader} is cast down by their own, and {town} is the free heart of the wilds.

roads.name: Iron Crown
roads.blurb: Rule by crown or iron: a town so firmly held that no bloc dares to stir and no foe finds a crack.
roads.title: The iron crown
roads.ending: {name}'s spies come to {town} looking for a malcontent to buy, a door left open, a councillor with a grudge, and find none: the watch is everywhere and the mayor's word is the only law. {leader} looks on a town that cannot be divided or frightened, and so do the wilds. One by one the halls that served {name} bend the knee to the crown of {town} instead.

roads.name: Capital of Adventurers
roads.blurb: The companies make your town their home and clear the map.
roads.title: The capital of adventurers
roads.ending: There is no lair left in the wilds the companies of {town} have not torn open. {name} has nowhere left to hide, and {leader} dies alone in the last of them.

roads.name: Merchant Crown
roads.blurb: Own the region's trade and starve the big bad's host.
roads.title: The merchant crown
roads.ending: Every road and river carries {town}'s goods and nobody else's. {name}'s host can buy neither bread nor blades; its sellswords take {town}'s coin instead, and {leader} is handed over in a sack.
